_rule: Appendix 2.1 and Equation (1): the outcome is the gross prior-year movement over the underwriting years u <= t-2 of the year t report's printed gross claims development table. An older-years column (such as '2013 and prior') is one of those mature years only if its last step (its latest cell less the cell before it, in the year t table) is a like-for-like movement of the same set of underwriting years during year t. Restated BY CALENDAR YEAR (the year t report recomputes the whole column for its coverage, so each cell is the total of the same years at one calendar date; the label is fixed, or the rows read 'n years or more later'): the last step is like for like and the column stays in. Built BY DEVELOPMENT AGE (the year t cell at age a is the year t-1 report's older column at age a plus the underwriting year that joined the block, so its coverage grows by one year each report): the last step mixes calendar dates, so the column is left out. A column with no development of its own (a single figure, or one the stored grid does not carry) is not part of the triangle and is left out. rule_figure_m is the figure the test gives, adopted_figure_m the figure the primary adopts, and consistent says whether the two are the same figure (the adopted figure treats the column as the rule does; null where the construction is undeterminable, so there is no single rule figure); agrees_within_tolerance is the readers' looser test, within 0.5m or 1% (for an undeterminable construction, within it of every candidate figure). The structured fields (construction, last_step_like_for_like, rule_includes_column, rule_figure_m, consistent) follow the readers' construction by the rule and nothing else. One record is the exception: 1200_2017 is adopted against the rule as the readers apply it (the column stays in, 44.9, where the rule leaves it out, 40.5). Its structured fields carry the readers' view (rule_includes_column false, rule_figure_m 40.5, consistent false); adopted_by_decision is true and decision_override records the figure adopted and the decision, a decision of the Claude analysis session, 23 October 2026. A record whose construction, or whose application of the rule, could not be settled is marked confidence 'low_confidence'; its adopted figure stands (a decision of the Claude analysis session, 23 October 2026).

_population.how_chosen: The measurement (round2/measurement/aggcol.json and report.md) scanned all 1,065 record files of the corpus for an older-years ('& prior') column. Part A: records whose stored gross RAG triangle carries the column (aggregated_cohort), 24 in the primary sample. Part B: records whose extraction notes say the filing's table has an older-years column the stored grid leaves out, 47 in the primary sample. Primary sample only: records outside it (510_2014, 557_2014, 2468_2016, 4020_2017, 5678_2015 and other records of the 672 construction alone) were not read. The 64 records read are the 17 of Part A in the primary that the measurement did not settle by its own cell test, and all 47 of Part B. Each was read by one reader of the X arm and one of the Y arm, independently (round 2 of 23 October 2026); the 13 records on which the arms could not settle the construction or disagreed were read again by the tie-break readers Z1 and Z2 (round 3).
_population.part_a_not_read_again_why: 218_2016 to 218_2020: the measurement's cell test found the column calendar-restated (cells equal, rows labelled 'n years or more later'), consistent with the adopted figure. 1945_2023 and 1945_2024: left out of the figure since the author's decision of 22 October 2026 (readings F1, F2; data/mature_cohort_figures.json), and read again by Z1 and Z2 as development_age.
_population.section_c_why: 12 records whose first stored column's age-0 cell is more than 2.5 times its neighbours' (probably individual large underwriting years, not aggregated columns); the measurement did not find a printed older-years column for them and they were not read

decision_override.text: Decision of the Claude analysis session, 23 October 2026: the column stays in (44.9), against the rule as the readers apply it (40.5), because its second-to-last cell equals the end-2016 calendar total (UY2010 266.9 at ages 5 and 6 in the 2016 report), so the last step holds only 2017 movements, and leaving the column out would drop UY2011's 2017 movement. The rule's application to this column could not be settled, so the record is low confidence.
